body:
Prompt injection risk: Job descriptions from external feeds (Indeed RSS) are entity-decoded here and flow into job.description, which the popup can send to Gemini for summarization/cleanup (SUMMARIZE_JD/transformJobText). Because the untrusted posting text is embedded directly into the prompt, a malicious feed item can include adversarial instructions that conflict with the system’s intended instruction and steer the model’s output. --- Best fix: sanitize untrusted job-description text for LLM safety before it can be reused downstream, while preserving existing functionality for UI/search as much as possible.

In lib/job-search.js, within normalizeIndeedJob, keep the entity decoding for extraction accuracy but add a defensive sanitization step that strips common prompt-injection markers and instruction-like control phrases from the decoded feed text before it is used further. Then use this sanitized text for downstream description normalization. This reduces risk without changing endpoint behavior or parsing flow structure.

Concretely:

  • Add a small local helper function in normalizeIndeedJob (or right above it) to neutralize common adversarial prompt tokens/phrases (e.g., “ignore previous instructions”, “system:”, “assistant:”, XML-like instruction wrappers).
  • After line 901, apply this sanitizer to decodedDescription.
  • Use the sanitized value where description content is derived for normalized output and regex-based company extraction where applicable.
  • Keep fallbacks intact so functionality remains stable.

No new imports/dependencies are required.
